questions.title: How did DeepSeekMath collect its nearly‑120B‑token corpus?
questions.question_body:
"The authors describe an iterative pipeline beginning with OpenWebMath, training a fastText classifier
with positive samples sampled randomly (>512{}) issuing labels positives/negatives,
and then re‐ranking pages harvested from deduplicated Common Crawl.
I am confused about what quantitative stopping criteria were used:
* How frequently was the iteration rerun (>
four passes were made?)
and *why did they consider returning pages over 10 % collected
within a domain ‘math‐related’?
What precise metric led them finally cease mining after observing
~98 % overlap between iteration 3 and iteration 4?”

questions.title: "Ten‑gram Exact Matching Criterion Clarification"
questions.question_body:
"During de‑contamination section the authors invoke "exact matches larger than ten grams" against MATH/GSM8K benchmarks.
Is ten grams arbitrarily chosen?
Moreover how do shorter (<10 g) fragments get removed?
Do authors risk discarding useful material arising merely due
to insufficient substring overlap?
And why apply different treatment when benchmark phrases
are shorter than ten grams versus longer?”

questions.title: "Code Training’s Role in Mathematical Reasoning Gains"
questions.question_body:
"Subsection ‘Lessons Learnt’ compares two‐stage (>code →math) versus one‐stage mixed (>code+math).
Table data indicates modest gains when Python tools are involved,
but seemingly negligible or even adverse impact on pure CoT accuracy.
Is this drop caused mainly by parameter capacity saturation at one‐block models (≈1 B params)
or by semantic interference caused by overlapping token distributions?
Which evidence makes authors assert “catastrophic forgetting” occurs when code tokens precede math training?”

questions.title: "Arxiv Papers Deleterious Influence on Math Benchmarks"
questions.question_body:
"Authors claim models trained exclusively on arXiv scraping perform worse or show little gain.
Given arXiv contains clean TeX mathematics,
basic intuition suggests extra scientific material should help.
Could sparsity/noise issues arising from macro stripping
(ArXiV‐RedPajama workflow) explain reduced performance?
Is there evidence arXiv examples match task distribution poorly,
either stylistically or linguistically?”

questions.title: "Baseline Replacement via Group Scores Instead Of Critic Functions"
questions.question_body:
"In Eq.(5), GRPO eliminates critic networks entirely.
Instead an agent samples G outputs per prompt;
the mean reward over that group serves simultaneously
as negative and positive baseline.
Intuitively my trouble:
since rewards come purely from terminal scoring devices,
could replacing expectation estimated by a learned Vψ cripple variance reduction?
some literature prefer agent‐specific baselines;
how effective isthe merely averaging description?”
